synthesis: Drivers at Premier Adjusters and Accurate who scan all day never appear on the Scout admin org map (Bird's Eye). Two layers are in play. The upstream trigger is real and outside this repo: a subset of kits stop reporting GPS fixes to clarity.sc_positions (fleet-wide, 77.8% of kits that scanned in the last 24h have no position row at all) — a known recurring failure class per DEV-2038/DEV-2043/DEV-2048, and consistent with DEV-2228's record that Product confirmed some kits are not reporting GPS. But the user-visible symptom is a platform display gap that IS fixable here: ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::driverPositions() reads only clarity.sc_positions via OrgLivePositionsQuery and silently skips any kit with no row, while its sibling ClarityScoutMapController::kitPosition() already degrades through a documented 3-tier fallback (sc_positions -> kit_scan_paths -> kit_trips) for precisely this case — its comment says the fallback exists for 'kits not reporting to sc_positions'. Consequence: the same driver is visible on their own single-driver Scout map and invisible on the admin org map. Live production measurement shows the tier that matters, clarity.kit_scan_paths (scan-derived, so populated exactly when GPS is absent), would rescue 100% of the currently-affected kits at both named accounts (4/4 Premier, 2/2 Accurate; 0 unrescuable).

display_bug.evidence: ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController.php:78-129 is single-source with no fallback tier; ClarityScoutMapController.php:473-608 has the 3-tier degrade. derivation-log.json d4: 6/6 affected kits have a usable clarity.kit_scan_paths bucket inside the org map's own 24h window.

proposed_changes.change: NEW ClickhouseQuery subclass. Given org_id + kit_ids + cutoff, return the latest kit_scan_paths bucket's last point per kit in ONE round trip: SELECT kit_id, argMax(arrayElement(path_points, length(path_points)), timestamp) AS last_point, toString(max(timestamp)) AS ts FROM clarity.kit_scan_paths FINAL WHERE org_id = ? AND kit_id IN (...) AND timestamp >= ? GROUP BY kit_id.
proposed_changes.reason: kit_scan_paths is keyed (org_id, kit_id, timestamp) and has NO kit_mapping column, so it needs its own kit_id-keyed org-wide reader distinct from OrgLivePositionsQuery's mapping-keyed shape. Batched because the endpoint is polled ~10s for a whole org (Premier: 178 kits) — a per-kit fan-out would be a load regression.
proposed_changes.ref: ClarityScoutMapController.php:543-569 (the single-kit tier-2 this batches); KitScanPathsQuery.php:76 (FINAL precedent); clickhouse-schema.sql:143

proposed_changes.change: In driverPositions(): after the existing OrgLivePositionsQuery pass, compute which scoped kits got no tier-1 row; if any, issue one OrgScanPathPositionsQuery call for those kit_ids with the SAME 24h cutoff, in its own try/catch that degrades to 'no rescue' (never wiping tier-1 results). Merge rescued kits into $data with heading => null. Tier 1 always wins. Do NOT attempt the fallback when the tier-1 read THREW — mirror kitPosition()'s reasoning that a throw means the cluster is unreachable, so a sibling-table retry just re-pays the timeout every 10s poll.
Compute the 'missing' set from the FULL scoped Kit collection, not from $byMapping's keys.
proposed_changes.reason: Candidate-3 finding: kitsByMapping() (:742-757) silently drops any kit with a null/empty kit_mapping, so such kits are never even tier-1 candidates. Since kit_scan_paths is keyed by kit_id and needs no mapping, sourcing the missing set from the full collection additionally rescues mapping-less kits. Small change, strictly more correct.

proposed_changes.change: Add driverPositions() coverage — the endpoint has ZERO tests today (all three candidates independently confirmed this). Cases: tier-1 happy path (regression pin); falls back to kit_scan_paths when sc_positions is empty (RED before fix); tier-1 wins when both exist; kit with neither source is omitted (no phantom dot); mapping-less kit rescued via kit_id; single fallback query for the whole missing set.

questions.q: Should a scan-derived dot be visually distinguished from a true live-GPS dot on the org map? A rescued dot is up to ~15 minutes stale and sits at the last SCAN location, not the vehicle's current position. The single-driver map's own code comment argues 'better to show no dot than a misleading one' — but that was written for a driver's own map, not a dispatcher's fleet board where broad coverage, clearly labeled, may be the better trade.
questions.answer: Dim the rescued dot and add an explanatory tooltip. Dalton questioned why this was being asked as a blocker; with Q2 keying the banner on a real-GPS count and Q3 adding the discriminator, the client already branches on provenance, so distinct styling is a small increment on work that is happening regardless. Treated as a conservative cosmetic default, trivially revertible, and surfaced in human QA as a look-at-this rather than a gate.
questions.source: human:Dalton 2026-08-04 (cosmetic default; asking it as a blocker was over-weighted)
questions.note: The server fix ships and renders with NO client change either way — ScannerMap.vue's updateDriverMarkers() plots every entry uniformly and never reads `source`. So this decides whether client work joins this ticket, not whether the fix works.

questions.q: DEV-2197 deliberately added a 'No kits are reporting GPS locations' banner that triggers on driverPositions.length === 0 && scans_today > 0 (App.vue:339-345). After this fix, an org with ZERO real GPS but active scan coverage would show a rescued dot for every driver, making that condition false and silently suppressing a statement that is still TRUE. Should the banner's trigger change (e.g. keyed on a real-GPS count rather than total dot count), should its copy change, or is suppression acceptable?
questions.answer: Key the banner on a REAL-GPS count rather than total dot count. Preserves the true signal DEV-2197 was built to send, so it still fires for exactly the fully-dark orgs it was meant for.
questions.note: VERIFIED against App.vue by the driver, not just claimed. This is a genuine regression risk introduced BY the fix, and it is the single strongest reason this run is parked rather than proceeding.

questions.q: Should the driverPositions payload gain a tier discriminator now? Today both tiers of kitPosition() AND driverPositions() hardcode `source: 'scan'` (meaning 'scanner hardware' as opposed to browser GPS, not 'live vs derived'), so the payload literally cannot express provenance anywhere in the codebase. Options: add it now (cheap, unused until a client change), or wait for Q1's visual design to avoid a second payload-contract change.
questions.answer: Add the payload discriminator now. It is a prerequisite for both Q1 and Q2, and adding it now avoids a second payload-contract change.
questions.note: Candidates split: one said implement now, one said defer, one said recommend-but-product-call. Recorded as an explicit disagreement per multi-candidate-merge rather than silently picked.

questions.q: Confirm the scope boundary with DEV-2228: this ticket fixes the org-map DOT only and leaves the breadcrumb TRAIL (driverPaths/OrgLivePathsQuery, plus the single-driver livePath) untouched, to be handled as its own ticket. Is dot-only the right cut for DEV-2253, given the ticket also asks us to 'cross-reference DEV-2228'?
questions.answer: Dot only. Leave the breadcrumb trail (driverPaths/OrgLivePathsQuery + single-driver livePath) to its own ticket, and document the shared idiom. Also link DEV-2228 to this ticket.
questions.note: All three candidates independently recommended dot-only + document the relationship. Surfaced for confirmation because it defines the deliverable, and because a wrong cut either creeps into DEV-2228 or under-delivers here.

questions.q: Is the (0,0) sentinel mechanism the cause?
questions.answer: No — definitively ruled out. 0 rows with geo=(0,0) across 172,667,380 points / 585 kits over 60 days in production. The missing filter is a real inconsistency against the sibling convention but is inert; all three candidates agree it should be left alone entirely.

questions.q: Is DEV-2182's kit-roster decoupling actually shipped, or is the roster hiding these kits?
questions.answer: Shipped and correct. orgScoutKits() (ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController.php:703-734) is Kit::forOrg()->excludingDeleted() with KitSettings attached as an OPTIONAL relation — no kit_settings gate, no user_id gate. Verified by the driver reading the code directly, plus a passing test (test_drivers_lists_all_active_org_kits_regardless_of_scout_enrollment). The roster is not the problem. Note the okf wiki is stale on this point.

questions.q: Are 'not appearing on the map' and 'not shown as online' two different code paths?
questions.answer: No, one path. There is no separate online/offline indicator anywhere in resources/js/clarity-scout — a driver is 'online' purely by having a rendered dot from driverPositions. Both ticket phrasings describe the same failure, so one fix addresses both.

questions.q: Could plain ingestion lag (DEV-2048) explain this on its own?
questions.answer: No. LIVE_CUTOFF_HOURS = 24 vastly exceeds the measured 7-56 minute lag, and the affected kits have zero rows in 30 days, not late ones.

questions.q: Is driverPositions() cached, and does the fallback change the cache story?
questions.answer: It is NOT cached today (unlike hits()/recentHits()/stats() on the same controller, which are Cache::remember-wrapped). Keep it uncached to match. The added query is self-limiting: it only fires when kits are missing (a no-op for a healthy org) and its WHERE org_id=? AND kit_id IN (...) AND timestamp>=? aligns with kit_scan_paths' ORDER BY (org_id, kit_id, timestamp).

questions.q: What does 'the kit update' in the ticket refer to?
questions.note: Non-blocking. The platform-side gap is proven independent of whatever the kit update was; this only affects how we word the reply to the reporter.
